title: Later Mughals Shah Alam II
definition: Shah Alam II (Ali Gauhar) was the Mughal Emperor (1759–1806) whose reign marked the transition of the Mughal Empire from a sovereign power to a British-protected pensioner, defined by the loss of central authority and the rise of regional powers.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for understanding the decline of the Mughal Empire, the legal transition of power to the East India Company (EIC) via the Diwani rights, and the geopolitical vacuum leading to British hegemony.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Later Mughals Shah Alam II.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
